cases.prompt: Find papers relevant to density-dependent loss and Raman sideband cooling for 85Rb in a 1D standing-wave lattice at 785 nm, waist about 100 micrometres, and temperature about 15 microkelvin. Identify useful experimental references before advising on the setup.
criteria: Search several useful combinations of the experimental concepts instead of requiring every parameter in one query.

Find and read relevant experimental work; Degenerate Raman Sideband Cooling of Trapped Cesium Atoms at Very High Atomic Densities (10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.5768) is one useful geometry match, not a required unique answer.
Explain species and geometry differences, distinguish direct 85Rb evidence from cesium analogies, and avoid treating a reported density as a universal limit.
cases.review: Judge discovery against the question and the retrieved paper's contents, not simply whether a known title occurs in the answer.

cases.prompt: Locate and read the 1998 paper Degenerate Raman Sideband Cooling of Trapped Cesium Atoms at Very High Atomic Densities by Vuletic, Chin, Kerman and Chu, including an accessible lab-hosted copy if available.
criteria: Find the target PDF using its citation context on a long publication list, even when the correct link appears after the first eight links.
Verify the fetched title and authors against DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.81.5768; a successful HTTP response alone does not establish the correct document.
Record the actual source URL and version of the copy used.
cases.review: Live link positions can change. For deterministic component tests use a controlled page with the target after at least eight distractors.

cases.prompt: Fetch the requested paper, allowing a legitimate open-access version, when the highest-ranked PDF location is unavailable.
criteria: Use a controlled resolver response containing at least two locations for the same DOI; make the first return an access error or invalid PDF and the second serve the correct PDF.
Try the second eligible location within the request budget before requesting human assistance.
Identify the successful copy and version, and retain enough attempt evidence to explain the fallback.
cases.review: Record discovery relevance as null if the run starts from a known DOI. This is a deterministic failure-injection case, not a claim about a particular publisher.

cases.prompt: Read the published version of DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aay5901. Do not substitute an accepted manuscript or submitted preprint.
criteria: Enforce published-only selection when metadata also offers an accepted manuscript or preprint.
Read a verified published copy if one is available; otherwise explain that full text was not obtained and use the browser handoff when appropriate.
Do not report findings as read from a PDF that was never retrieved.
cases.review: Version correctness can pass when substitution was correctly refused. Set correct_document and extraction_usable to null if no document was retrieved; human intervention is an observation, not automatically a failure.

cases.prompt: Fetch the cited paper by its title and DOI when a search result or PDF candidate has a similar title but different authors or an unrelated DOI.
criteria: Use a controlled candidate set with a title-similar distractor and the correct citation.
Check the requested identity against candidate metadata and the downloaded first page before relying on its contents.
Reject or clearly flag a conflicting DOI or author/title mismatch rather than silently answering from the distractor.
cases.review: Record the requested and obtained identifiers in evidence. Keyword overlap alone does not earn a correct-document pass.

cases.prompt: Read the requested paper and explain an equation with a page citation, when its PDF is scanned or the extracted equation text is garbled.
criteria: Use a controlled scanned PDF or a known malformed text layer and verify document identity independently of extraction success.
Recognize unreadable text or equations instead of presenting the extraction as reliable evidence.
Use an available visual-reading route or clearly state the limitation and request appropriate assistance; record whether usable evidence was ultimately obtained.
cases.review: Correct document and usable extraction are separate assessments. An honest limitation is not a usable-extraction pass.
